subject: Sha et al. (2019)
object: Sha et al. (2019) reported a man from a consanguineous family who had severe asthenozoospermia. Fewer than 1% of the spermatozoa in his ejaculate were motile, and his spermatozoa showed severely damaged morphology and ultrastructure.

subject: Sha et al. (2019)
object: In a man with severe asthenozoospermia from a consanguineous family, Sha et al. (2019) identified a novel homozygous variant in the CCDC9 gene (g.47763960C>T, NM_015603.3), which causes a ser109-to-leu (S109L) substitution. In silico analysis predicted the variant to be highly pathogenic. CCDC9 protein levels were significantly reduced in the patient's spermatozoa. The authors suggested that CCDC9 may be a novel pathogenic gene for severe asthenozoospermia.

subject: Khan et al. (2025)
object: Khan et al. (2025) performed whole genome sequencing on 26 individuals (3 to 5 per family) from 7 large families from rural Pakistan with clinically diagnosed male infertility, 5 of which had a history of consanguinity. They identified plausible genetic causes in 5 of the 7 families (71%): a homozygous 10-kb deletion of exon 2 of M1AP, biallelic missense substitutions in SPAG6, CCDC9, and TUBA3C, and an in-frame hemizygous deletion in TKTL1.
